title: Clearing denominators of sections on the nonvanishing locus, qcqs case
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] (the intersection of any two affine opens is quasi-compact), $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $X_s=\{x\in X:s(x)\ne0\text{ in }\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)\}$, where $\kappa(x)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. For every $u\in\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal F)$ there exist $m\ge0$ and $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$ such that $t|_{X_s}=u\otimes(s|_{X_s})^{\otimes m}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (label lemma-invert-s-sections), proof of part (2): surjectivity of the canonical localization map

proof.text: At each point choose a Zariski neighbourhood on which $\mathcal L$ is free by [def-sc-invertible-module], and an affine neighbourhood on which $\mathcal F$ is a tilde module by [pqf-def-coherent]. Choose a principal open inside the affine presentation neighbourhood and the trivializing neighbourhood; [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] identifies the restriction of the tilde module there with the localization of its presenting module, so both properties hold on this principal open. These opens cover $X$, so quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] gives a finite subcover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^r V_i$ on which both properties hold. Write $e_i$ for a generator and $s|_{V_i}=f_i e_i$. For a point of $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, the image of $s$ in $\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)$ is nonzero exactly when $f_i\notin\mathfrak p_x$; hence $X_s\cap V_i=D(f_i)$. Write $\mathcal F|_{V_i}=\widetilde M_i$; identifying $M_i$ with $\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal F)$ by the $r=1$ case of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], that same node identifies $\Gamma(D(f_i),\mathcal F)$ with $(M_i)_{f_i}$. Write $u|_{D(f_i)}=v_i/f_i^{a_i}$, choose $a\ge a_i$ for every $i$, and set $w_i=f_i^{a-a_i}v_i\otimes e_i^{\otimes a}\in\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes a})$. Then $w_i|_{D(f_i)}=u|_{D(f_i)}\otimes s^{\otimes a}$. Identify the specified nonvanishing open with the complement of the zero-locus support using [lem-weil-pbc-section-nonvanishing-zero-locus], so basicOpen_coeff_eq supplies the chart equality.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), part (2), finite trivializing cover and local fractions

proof.text: Quasi-separatedness makes W_ij = V_i intersect V_j quasi-compact. The difference d_ij of the two local twisted lifts restricts to zero on W_ij intersect X_s by Step 1. The basis E_i of L^a on V_i identifies d_ij uniquely with dprime_ij tensor E_i for a section dprime_ij of F on W_ij. Tensoring with the restricted basis is injective, so dprime_ij vanishes on D(f_i|W_ij). Apply [pqf-lem-qcoh-compact-section-power-torsion] to F on the compact open W_ij to obtain f_i^b_ij dprime_ij = 0. Tensoring back with E_i gives f_i^b_ij d_ij = 0. This uses quasi-coherence only for F, not for the twisted module, and does not require affine overlaps.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), part (2), compatibility on quasi-compact overlaps

proof.text: Take the maximum b of the finitely many b_ij, with b=0 when the index set is empty. Let z_i be the image of w_i under mulTensorPowSection s F a b. On each overlap, tensorPowSectionOne s b is the restricted basis E_i^b multiplied by f_i^b; mulTensorPowSection_app_eq_zero and f_i^b d_ij = 0 show that z_i and z_j agree. Glue z_i by the sheaf axiom to a global section u of F tensor L^(a+b). The identity mulTensorPowSection_app_tmulSection and Step 1 show that u restricts to t tensor s^(a+b) on each V_i intersect X_s. Sheaf uniqueness on their cover of X_s proves the required equality.

split_report.summary: Proved the qcqs clearing-denominators statement by finitely many affine charts with simultaneous line-bundle trivializations and module presentations, affine module localization, power-torsion on each quasi-compact overlap, and gluing. The overlap step uses the existing restriction-torsion statement for quasi-coherent modules and does not assume affine intersections. No new nodes were needed.
